planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil; this cascading hydrangea blooms on old wood, so avoid pruning except to remove dead stems.

directions: Fairytrail Bride is a trailing, cascade-habit hydrangea that sets clear white, frilly deckle-edged flowers densely along its arching stems rather than only at the tips. Grow it with four to six hours of sun, favoring morning light with afternoon shade in hot regions, and let it drape over a container edge, retaining wall, or hanging basket. Deadheading is not necessary and pruning should be minimal since flowers form on old wood.

common_name: Let's Dance Big Easy Hydrangea (Reblooming Color-Shifting Bigleaf Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil; this compact mophead reblooms on new wood after the old-wood flush, so light pruning is tolerated.

directions: Let's Dance Big Easy packs oversized mophead blooms onto a compact, mounded frame, with flowers that emerge green, shift to pink or lavender depending on soil pH, and often fade back toward green as they age. It sets buds on both old and new wood, giving a mid-summer flush followed by continued rebloom into early fall without the heavy pruning larger mopheads require. Its small size suits foundation plantings and large containers, and it tolerates coastal salt exposure better than many bigleaf hydrangeas.

common_name: Let's Dance Hot Stepper Hydrangea (Cold-Hardy Reblooming White-Veined Hydrangea)
scientific_name: Hydrangea macrophylla x serrata 'Let's Dance Hot Stepper'

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil; this hybrid reblooms on both old and new wood, so cold-damaged old growth still produces flowers from new stems.

directions: Let's Dance Hot Stepper is a cold-hardy macrophylla x serrata cross that opens pink mophead blooms edged with fine white veining, turning blue with acidic soil or aluminum sulfate amendment. Mature flowers darken while fresh blooms and lime-green buds open alongside them, giving a two-tone effect through summer and fall. Because it flowers on both old and new wood, it is more forgiving of harsh winters than older bigleaf hydrangeas, and it holds up well in borders, containers, and cut arrangements.

common_name: Sonic Bloom Ghost Weigela (Reblooming Gold-Foliage Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil; prune lightly right after the main spring flush since the heaviest bloom forms on old wood.

directions: Sonic Bloom Ghost pairs the repeat-flowering habit of the Sonic Bloom series with foliage that opens lime green and glows gold through the season, giving the shrub ongoing color interest between bloom flushes of bright pink-red, trumpet-shaped flowers. It blooms heavily in late spring on old wood, then sends up sporadic new flowers in late summer and early fall on new growth, extending interest well beyond a single season's shrubs. It resists deer browsing and common foliage diseases, making it a low-fuss choice for borders, groupings, or large containers.

common_name: Shadowland Echo the Sun Hosta (Chartreuse Ruffled-Margin Hosta)

planting.note: Divide or plant bare-root/potted crowns in spring or fall into moist, humus-rich, organically enriched soil; avoid more than about four hours of direct sun to prevent leaf scorch.

directions: Echo the Sun holds bright chartreuse-yellow, wedge-shaped leaves with thick substance and a gently rippled margin, forming a low, spreading mound that brightens dim corners of a shade bed. Lavender flowers rise on scapes well above the foliage in mid-summer and draw hummingbirds. Give it consistently moist, organically enriched soil and limit direct sun to the cooler morning hours, since excess light fades the gold coloring and risks leaf burn.

common_name: Shadowland Love Story Hosta (Creamy-Centered Chartreuse-Jetted Hosta)

planting.note: Divide or plant crowns in spring or fall into average to fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil; clean away dead foliage after frost to deter overwintering slugs.

directions: Love Story carries long, heart-shaped leaves with green margins and chartreuse streaking that bleeds into creamy white centers, each edge finished with a piecrust-style wave. Its low, mounded habit makes it a strong filler among larger hostas or in a mixed container, and white flowers on tall scapes draw hummingbirds in early summer. Keep soil evenly moist through the growing season and watch for slug damage as new growth emerges in spring.

common_name: Shadowland Seducer Hosta (Dark Green Gold-Margined Hosta)

planting.note: Divide or plant crowns in spring or fall into humus-rich soil; it tolerates drier conditions once established better than many hosta cultivars.

directions: Seducer shows dark green leaves rimmed with a chartreuse-to-gold margin and a faint trace of white between center and edge, with the contrast intensifying as summer heat builds. Its upright, mounded habit and above-average drought tolerance make it useful as a border plant or landscape specimen where consistent irrigation is not guaranteed. Near-white to lavender flowers appear on tall scapes in late summer and attract hummingbirds.

common_name: Shadowland Voices in the Wind Hosta (Blue-Green Gold-Margined Ruffled Hosta)

planting.note: Divide or plant crowns in spring or fall into average to fertile, acidic to neutral soil kept evenly moist; limit direct sun to about four hours.

directions: Voices in the Wind pairs blue-green, wedge-shaped leaves with creamy yellow margins and a ruffled edge that gives ornamental texture even when the plant is not in bloom, bred from a parentage including 'Arctic Blast', 'Neptune', 'Winfield Blue', and 'Joy Ride'. Its low, wide-spreading mound works well as a container filler or a groundcover-style edging along a shaded path. Pale lavender flowers rise on scapes in mid-summer and draw hummingbirds to the bed.
